neighbours.label: Predicts 'cap' or 'lid' next: fires on the word just before a cap (baseball, polar ice, lens, screw-on, bottle), regardless of what actually follows; quiet where nothing sets up a cap.
fire: For the hike, my brother packed sunscreen and his favourite baseball cap.
Satellite images show the Greenland ice cap losing mass every summer.
The jars come with screw-on lids that keep the sauce fresh.
Every player on the team got a signed baseball hat after the final.
Climate models predict the polar ice will keep thinning this century.
He lost the lens cap somewhere on the beach.
She pried off the bottle cap with the edge of a spoon.
The containers have screw-top lids and fit neatly in the fridge.
quiet: For the hike, my brother packed sunscreen and his favourite wool socks.
Satellite images show the Greenland coastline changing every summer.
The jars come with printed labels that list the ingredients.
Every player on the team got a signed football shirt after the final.
Climate models predict the ocean currents will keep shifting this century.
He lost his sandals somewhere on the beach.
She sliced the bread with the edge of a knife.
The containers are made of glass and fit neatly in the fridge.

predictions: median fire ~0.45 (probes: baseball 0.69, screw-on 0.51, polar ice 0.40, lens 0.31); near misses < 0.15 (ice cream bowl 0.06, budget 0.003). 'baseball glove' still fired 0.46 at ' baseball', so near misses drop the cap-predicting word itself.
notes: Logit effect of the + pole suppresses ' cap'/' lid'; the - pole is the cap predictor. Causal: it reads the setup word, not the cap.
